ov: More than 8,000 species of long-horned relatives of grasshoppers, also called bush crickets. Many are green and leaf-shaped, live in trees and call loudly on summer nights. Their thread-like antennae, which can be longer than the body, tell them apart from grasshoppers.

why.dg: Harmless, though large ones can give a painful bite or pinch if handled; it seldom breaks the skin.
why.et: Some species are eaten, such as the nsenene of Uganda and neighbouring areas.

df: Most eat leaves, flowers, bark and seeds, but many species hunt insects, snails or even small lizards.
fx: The name copies the loud three-part "ka-ty-did" song of a North American species.
Some nymphs mimic ants, spiders or assassin bugs until they are big enough to escape predators.
